title: Moving in
subtitle: Trasloco e vita da inquilina
intro: September. Chiara and Sofia share a basement apartment in Bloordale: Mrs. Oyelaran's lease, Franco's van, an afternoon at IKEA, and the furnace that dies the first cold night. Chiara writes her first formal complaint email and discovers she had never actually read the lease. This unit opens B1 with the [[past perfect]] (I had / I'd done), the small revolution that is reported requests (she asked me to…), the vocabulary of a rental in Ontario, and the phrasal verbs of a house.
objectives: Narrate past events with a prior one: [[when I got home, the heat had died]], [[I had never signed a lease before]]
Report requests and orders: [[she asked me to turn down the heat]], [[he told me not to flush paper]]
Describe rental and heating problems and request repairs: [[the furnace isn't working]], [[when can you come to fix it?]]
Write a short formal complaint email: [[I am writing with regard to…]], [[I would be grateful if…]]
Use household and moving phrasal verbs: [[move in / out, set up, turn on / off, plug in, pick up, put away, throw out, break down]]
canDo: B1 · Spoken production: can describe a complex sequence of past events, including a prior one.
B1 · Spoken interaction: can report problems to a landlord and request repairs on the phone.
B1 · Reading: can read the key clauses of a standard Ontario lease and a notice from a landlord.
B1 · Writing: can write a formal complaint email with the right register and opening / closing.
B1 · Listening: can follow a landlord's instructions about appliances, waste pickup and heating.

sections.title: Keys and a lease
sections.intro: Saturday morning. Mrs. Oyelaran, the landlord, hands Chiara two keys and a six-page lease. Franco's van is double-parked. Listen for the past perfect (I had never signed, we had already paid) and for the reported requests (she asked me to…, she told me not to…).

blocks.title: The keys
blocks.setting: Saturday 2 September, 10 a.m. 42 Lansdowne Avenue, Bloordale, basement entrance at the back. Chiara with Sofia, Mrs. Oyelaran at the door with a brown envelope. Franco's van blocking the alley. Overcast; the first cold morning of the fall.

lines.t: Good morning. You must be Chiara. Sofia, hi again. Come in. I've been waiting for you both. Did you have a hard time finding the back entrance?
lines.n: Buongiorno. Tu devi essere Chiara. Sofia, ciao di nuovo. Entrate. Vi stavo aspettando. Avete avuto difficoltà a trovare l'ingresso sul retro?
lines.note: I've been waiting for you: present perfect continuous, from unit 16. The back entrance: an Ontario basement rental is often entered through the alley.

lines.t: Not really. I'd been here last week with Sofia for the viewing. Franco found the alley right away. He parked the van outside — I hope that's okay for ten minutes.
lines.n: Non proprio. Ero stata qui la settimana scorsa con Sofia per visitare. Franco ha trovato il vicolo subito. Ha parcheggiato il furgone fuori — spero vada bene per dieci minuti.
lines.note: I'd been here last week: past perfect (I had been). I'd = I had. Prior to this moment of handover.

lines.t: Ten minutes is fine; after that the neighbour on the right starts shouting. Here's the lease, two copies. I've printed everything. Please read it before you sign; last year a tenant signed without reading and then {{he|she}} discovered we don't allow a washing machine on the second floor.
lines.n: Dieci minuti vanno bene; dopo il vicino di destra inizia a urlare. Ecco il contratto, due copie. Ho stampato tutto. Leggetelo prima di firmare; l'anno scorso un inquilino ha firmato senza leggere e poi ha scoperto che non consentiamo la lavatrice al secondo piano.
lines.note: Last year a tenant signed… then they discovered: past simple + past simple, two events in order. One of English's few singular-they moments: Italian would mark the gender.

lines.t: I've never signed a lease before. In Italy my parents did it for me, back home I lived with Dora. Could you walk me through the main pages?
lines.n: Non ho mai firmato un contratto prima. In Italia mia madre l'ha fatto per me, a casa vivevo da Dora. Potrebbe spiegarmi le pagine principali?
lines.note: I've never signed before: present perfect for life experience, unit 15. Could you walk me through: polite request, unit 14.

lines.t: Of course. This is the standard Ontario lease — the government introduced it a few years ago, so every landlord uses the same form. The rent is $1,650 a month, including hydro, water and heat. First and last month's up front; you've already paid that by e-transfer, I can see.
lines.n: Certo. Questo è il contratto standard dell'Ontario — il governo l'ha introdotto qualche anno fa, quindi tutti i proprietari usano lo stesso modulo. L'affitto è di 1.650 dollari al mese, incluse elettricità, acqua e riscaldamento. Primo e ultimo mese anticipato; l'avete già pagato con bonifico, vedo.
lines.note: You've already paid: present perfect — Oyelaran is linking the past action with the present moment. First and last up front: Ontario custom. Hydro = electricity in Ontario-speak.

lines.t: A few things before you sign. First: no washing machine in the unit, you use the one on the second floor. Second: no smoking anywhere. Third: don't flush any paper besides toilet paper — the pipes are from 1952 and I had to call a plumber twice last year because the previous tenant hadn't understood that.
lines.n: Alcune cose prima di firmare. Primo: niente lavatrice nel vostro appartamento, usate quella del secondo piano. Secondo: non si fuma da nessuna parte. Terzo: non buttate nel water altra carta oltre a quella igienica — i tubi sono del 1952 e l'anno scorso ho dovuto chiamare un idraulico due volte perché l'inquilina precedente non l'aveva capito.
lines.note: Had to call: past of have to (unit 12). The previous tenant hadn't understood: past perfect — a prior failure to understand. The three house rules.

lines.t: No washing machine. Got it. No smoking. Got it. Only toilet paper. Got it. What about the furnace — Sofia told me there'd been problems last winter.
lines.n: Niente lavatrice. Capito. Niente fumo. Capito. Solo carta igienica. Capito. E il riscaldamento — Sofia mi ha detto che l'anno scorso c'erano stati problemi.
lines.note: There'd been problems = there had been problems: past perfect. Sofia had told her — reported, with past perfect inside.

lines.t: There'd been one problem: a leaking valve. We replaced the whole furnace in April. If anything happens, text me — don't call, I don't answer unknown numbers. 24 hours' notice if I need to come in, by law. For emergencies, immediately. Welcome. Any questions?
lines.n: C'era stato un problema solo: una valvola che perdeva. Abbiamo sostituito tutta la caldaia ad aprile. Se succede qualcosa, mandami un messaggio — non chiamare, non rispondo ai numeri sconosciuti. 24 ore di preavviso se devo entrare, per legge. Per le emergenze, subito. Benvenuta. Hai domande?
lines.note: There'd been one problem: past perfect. We replaced: past simple, finished event. If anything happens, text me: zero conditional for a rule. 24 hours' notice: Ontario law.

lines.t: One. The alley neighbour on the right. Should I introduce myself before Franco's van gets him started?
lines.n: Una. Il vicino del vicolo a destra. Dovrei presentarmi prima che il furgone di Franco lo faccia arrabbiare?
lines.note: Should I: advice, unit 12. Gets him started: an informal phrasal, lit. makes him begin — i.e. complaining.

lines.t: Yes. His name's Doug, no relation to the bakery Doug. He's fine if you bring him a loaf of bread the first time. He told me last year he hadn't had a decent neighbour in a decade. Low bar.
lines.n: Sì. Si chiama Doug, non è parente del Doug della panetteria. Va bene se gli porti un pane la prima volta. Mi ha detto l'anno scorso che non aveva avuto un vicino decente in dieci anni. Standard bassi.
lines.note: He told me he hadn't had: reported speech + past perfect — a prior absence. The Italian equivalent is pretty close.

notes.phrase: I'd been here last week · there'd been one problem · the previous tenant hadn't understood · he hadn't had a decent neighbour · we had already paid
notes.note: Five past perfects in Oyelaran's conversation. Prior actions in a past narrative. The 'd (I'd, there'd, he'd) is had.

notes.phrase: the standard Ontario lease · first and last month's up front · hydro, water, heat included · 24 hours' notice · emergencies immediately · landlord and tenant board
notes.note: The vocabulary and the law of a basement rental in Toronto.

notes.phrase: Sofia told me there'd been problems · he told me he hadn't had a decent neighbour · she said we don't allow
notes.note: Reported speech first contact: past simple inside becomes past perfect; present simple inside stays present or shifts to past. Full rules in unit 19.

blocks.title: The furnace
blocks.setting: Three weeks later. 24 September, late evening. The first cold night of the fall, 2°C. Chiara's basement bedroom, 14°C and dropping. Sofia at the kitchen table in a parka. The furnace that had been fine until an hour ago.
blocks.register: informal between flatmates, then formal to landlord by text

lines.t: Sofia. The furnace just died. The thermostat said 20, now it's 14 and the air coming out is cold.
lines.n: Sofia. La caldaia è appena morta. Il termostato segnava 20, ora è 14 e l'aria che esce è fredda.
lines.note: The furnace just died: just + past simple in North American English (also just + present perfect in British). Both are common.

lines.t: You've got to be kidding me. We'd just put the plants near the window — if it goes down to 10 overnight they'll die. Did you check the breaker?
lines.n: Ma stai scherzando. Avevamo appena messo le piante vicino alla finestra — se scende a 10 di notte muoiono. Hai controllato il quadro elettrico?
lines.note: You've got to be kidding: present perfect idiom. We'd just put: past perfect with just = had just. The planted-them was before the furnace died. Breaker = interruttore elettrico; also electrical panel.

lines.t: I checked everything. The breaker's fine, the thermostat has batteries, there's no gas leak. I'm texting Mrs. Oyelaran.
lines.n: Ho controllato tutto. L'interruttore è a posto, il termostato ha le batterie, non c'è fuga di gas. Mando un messaggio alla signora Oyelaran.
lines.note: I checked everything: past simple, four finished actions.

lines.t: «Hi Mrs. Oyelaran, sorry to text at this hour. The furnace stopped working around 10:30 p.m. The thermostat reads 14°C. Sofia and I checked the breaker and the batteries. Could you let us know what to do? Thanks, Chiara.»
lines.n: «Salve signora Oyelaran, mi scuso per l'ora. La caldaia ha smesso di funzionare verso le 22:30. Il termostato segna 14°C. Sofia e io abbiamo controllato l'interruttore e le batterie. Può farci sapere cosa fare? Grazie, Chiara.»
lines.note: The register of a late-night text to a landlord: polite, specific, with the exact facts and no complaints. Could you let us know: polite indirect.

lines.t: «Hi Chiara. Sorry — I'm not surprised, same model. I've just called Vince (my furnace guy); he'll be there at 7 a.m. Can you be home? Also, in the meantime, I'd suggested running the oven for ten minutes with the door open as a last resort; please don't — I had a tenant try that two winters ago and I almost lost the house. Open the taps a trickle so the pipes don't freeze.»
lines.n: «Ciao Chiara. Scusa — non mi sorprende, è lo stesso modello. Ho appena chiamato Vince (il mio tecnico); sarà lì alle 7. Puoi essere a casa? Nel frattempo, avevo suggerito di accendere il forno dieci minuti con lo sportello aperto come ultima risorsa; per favore, non farlo — due inverni fa un inquilino l'ha provato e ho quasi perso la casa. Apri i rubinetti a filo perché i tubi non gelino.»
lines.note: I'd suggested (had suggested) running: past perfect — Oyelaran is reporting what she had told other tenants. A tenant try that: a tenant tried that. Almost lost the house: past simple.

lines.t: «Also — Chiara, two things. First, text, don't phone — you did it right. Second, I asked Franco to look over your boiler room last month and he said the vents were fine. If Vince finds otherwise, I'll pay for a cleaning before November.»
lines.n: «Un'altra cosa — Chiara, due cose. Primo, mandare messaggio, non chiamare — hai fatto giusto. Secondo, avevo chiesto a Franco di dare un'occhiata al locale caldaia il mese scorso e aveva detto che le prese d'aria erano a posto. Se Vince trova altro, pago io una pulizia prima di novembre.»
lines.note: I asked Franco to look over: reported request (ask + object + to + inf). He said the vents were fine: reported statement with backshift. The two patterns of unit 19 previewed.

lines.t: Right. Now the formal email, for your file. You need to write it tomorrow morning — in case the furnace goes again, you'll have a record. Mrs. O. is great, but things get forgotten.
lines.n: Giusto. Ora l'email formale, per il tuo archivio. Devi scriverla domani mattina — nel caso la caldaia salti di nuovo, avrai una traccia. La signora O. è una brava persona, ma le cose si dimenticano.
lines.note: Need to write it tomorrow morning: necessity (unit 12). In case: for the eventuality that. Mrs. O.: North American abbreviation of a name.

lines.t: «Dear Mrs. Oyelaran, I am writing with regard to the furnace outage of September 24th. The furnace stopped working at approximately 10:30 p.m. The indoor temperature dropped to 14°C. We checked the breaker and the batteries, as instructed. Vince attended the premises at 7 a.m. on September 25th and found an igniter failure, which has now been replaced. I would be grateful if you could confirm this in writing, and if any further issue arises before November, I will contact you immediately. Best regards, Chiara Russo.»
lines.n: «Gentile signora Oyelaran, Le scrivo in merito al guasto della caldaia del 24 settembre. La caldaia ha smesso di funzionare verso le 22:30. La temperatura interna è scesa a 14°C. Abbiamo controllato il quadro elettrico e le batterie, come indicato. Vince è intervenuto nei locali alle 7 del 25 settembre e ha trovato un guasto all'accenditore, che è stato ora sostituito. Le sarei grata se potesse confermarlo per iscritto, e se dovessero sorgere ulteriori problemi prima di novembre, La contatterò immediatamente. Cordiali saluti, Chiara Russo.»
lines.note: The register of a formal complaint email: with regard to, approximately, as instructed, attended the premises, I would be grateful, cordial sign-off.

notes.phrase: the furnace just died · we'd just put the plants · I'd suggested running the oven · I asked Franco to look over · he said the vents were fine
notes.note: Past simple and past perfect side by side. The reported-request structure (asked + object + to + inf) and the reported-statement with backshift (vents are → vents were).

notes.phrase: with regard to · approximately · as instructed · attended the premises · I would be grateful if you could · Best regards
notes.note: The vocabulary of a formal complaint email. Learn these phrases as blocks.

notes.phrase: the breaker · the thermostat · the furnace · the vents · the igniter · hydro · a cleaning · an outage
notes.note: The vocabulary of a basement rental in Ontario: things you learn only when they break.

questions.q: Mrs. Oyelaran told Chiara to call her as soon as there was a problem.
questions.t: Text me — don't call, I don't answer unknown numbers.
questions.why: Oyelaran specifically asked Chiara to text, not call.

questions.q: «I'd just put the plants near the window» means:
options: I had just put the plants near the window.
I would put the plants near the window.
I had been putting the plants near the window.
questions.why: I'd = I had with the past participle (put). Past perfect.

questions.q: When Vince ___ (arrive), Chiara ___ (not sleep, past perfect) all night. He ___ (find) the problem in ten minutes.
questions.n: Quando Vince è arrivato, Chiara non aveva dormito tutta la notte. Ha trovato il problema in dieci minuti.

sections.title: A lease, a kitchen, phrasal verbs
sections.intro: Rental and tenancy words, appliances and heating, moving-in phrasal verbs, and the small vocabulary of complaints.

items.n: contratto di affitto

ex.t: I signed the lease on September 1st. It's for one year.
ex.n: Ho firmato il contratto il 1° settembre. È di un anno.

items.note: Also tenancy agreement. In Ontario, the standard lease is a government form.

items.n: proprietario, padrone di casa

ex.t: The landlord is Mrs. Oyelaran. She lives upstairs.
ex.n: La proprietaria è la signora Oyelaran. Vive al piano di sopra.

items.note: Landlord / landlady. In Ontario, both are landlord in official forms.

items.n: inquilino, affittuario

ex.t: The previous tenant hadn't understood the pipes.
ex.n: L'inquilino precedente non aveva capito i tubi.

items.note: Also renter.

items.n: affitto (mensile); affittare, prendere / dare in affitto

ex.t: The rent is $1,650 a month. We rent from Mrs. Oyelaran.
ex.n: L'affitto è di 1.650 dollari al mese. Affittiamo dalla signora Oyelaran.

items.note: Pay the rent / rent an apartment / rent out (as landlord).

items.n: deposito, caparra; in Ontario anche last month's rent

ex.t: First and last month's up front; no damage deposit allowed by law.
ex.n: Primo e ultimo mese anticipato; nessuna caparra per danni, per legge.

items.note: Ontario law: landlords can only ask last month's rent as a deposit — no damage deposit.

items.n: preavviso; avviso

ex.t: I need to give 60 days' notice before moving out.
ex.n: Devo dare 60 giorni di preavviso prima di andarmene.

items.note: 60 days to move out, 24 hours for the landlord to enter.

items.n: utenze (luce, gas, acqua)

ex.t: Rent includes utilities: hydro, gas and water.
ex.n: L'affitto include le utenze: elettricità, gas e acqua.

items.note: Hydro = electricity in Ontario-speak. Comes from Ontario Hydro, the old provincial utility.

items.n: custode, portiere (del palazzo)

ex.t: The super lives in the first apartment. Call him for the furnace.
ex.n: Il custode abita nel primo appartamento. Chiamalo per la caldaia.

items.note: Usually shortened to super. In small houses, there is no super: you call the landlord directly.

items.n: reclamo, lamentela

ex.t: I filed a formal complaint about the furnace.
ex.n: Ho presentato un reclamo formale sulla caldaia.

items.note: File / lodge / make a complaint. Complaint letter / email.

items.n: ente ontario per i reclami inquilino-proprietario (LTB)

ex.t: If the landlord won't fix it, you can go to the Landlord and Tenant Board.
ex.n: Se il proprietario non ripara, puoi rivolgerti al Landlord and Tenant Board.

items.note: The provincial authority. Decisions on rent, repairs, eviction.

items.n: caldaia (ad aria o acqua)

ex.t: The furnace died at 10:30 p.m.
ex.n: La caldaia è morta alle 22:30.

items.note: In Ontario most houses have forced-air gas furnaces. Pronounced /ˈfɜːrnɪs/.

items.n: termostato

ex.t: Set the thermostat to 20°C during the day, 17 at night.
ex.n: Imposta il termostato a 20°C di giorno, 17 di notte.

items.note: Set / adjust / program the thermostat.

items.n: elettricità (Ontario-speak)

ex.t: The hydro bill comes every two months.
ex.n: La bolletta della luce arriva ogni due mesi.

items.note: Only in Ontario, Quebec and BC. In other provinces: electricity, power. In Italian: luce.

items.n: scaldabagno, scaldacqua

ex.t: The water heater is in the basement, next to the furnace.
ex.n: Lo scaldabagno è in cantina, accanto alla caldaia.

items.note: Also hot water tank. Often rented from a utility company.

items.n: interruttore automatico, salvavita

ex.t: If a plug blows, flip the breaker in the panel.
ex.n: Se salta una presa, aziona l'interruttore nel quadro.

items.note: The electrical panel = il quadro elettrico. Flip / reset the breaker. In British English: trip switch.

items.n: tubo, tubazione

ex.t: Open the taps a trickle so the pipes don't freeze.
ex.n: Apri i rubinetti a filo perché i tubi non gelino.

items.note: Water pipe / gas pipe. Pipes freeze and burst in Ontario winters.

items.n: elettrodomestico

ex.t: The appliances are included: fridge, stove, dishwasher.
ex.n: Gli elettrodomestici sono inclusi: frigorifero, cucina, lavastoviglie.

items.note: In Italian a single word: elettrodomestico. English uses appliance for the big ones, device for electronics.

items.n: frigorifero

ex.t: The fridge is empty but the freezer still has ice.
ex.n: Il frigo è vuoto ma il congelatore ha ancora del ghiaccio.

items.note: Short for refrigerator. Freezer: the separate frozen compartment.

items.n: cucina (fornelli e forno)

ex.t: The stove is gas; the oven is electric.
ex.n: La cucina è a gas; il forno è elettrico.

items.note: Also range. The oven = il forno; the burners = i fornelli.

items.n: spazzatura, rifiuti

ex.t: Garbage pickup is Thursday mornings in our zone.
ex.n: La raccolta rifiuti è il giovedì mattina nella nostra zona.

items.note: Also trash (US), rubbish (UK). Garbage can / garbage truck / garbage day.

items.n: raccolta differenziata (riciclabili)

ex.t: Blue bin for recycling, green bin for organics, grey bin for garbage.
ex.n: Bidone blu per i riciclabili, verde per l'umido, grigio per l'indifferenziato.

items.note: Three bins in Toronto. The green bin is for organic waste.

items.n: tirare lo sciacquone

ex.t: Don't flush any paper besides toilet paper.
ex.n: Non buttare nel water altra carta oltre a quella igienica.

items.note: Also flush (noun) = lo sciacquone. The flush: a scarica.

items.n: trasferirsi (in casa), entrare (in casa)

ex.t: We moved in on September 1st, Franco's day off.
ex.n: Siamo entrate il 1° settembre, il giorno libero di Franco.

items.note: Opposite: move out. Also move in with = andare a vivere con.

items.n: montare, mettere su, configurare

ex.t: I set up the IKEA shelves on Saturday afternoon.
ex.n: Ho montato gli scaffali IKEA sabato pomeriggio.

items.note: Separable: I set them up. Also set up a bank account, set up Wi-Fi.

items.n: accendere / spegnere

ex.t: Turn on the furnace, turn off the lights.
ex.n: Accendi la caldaia, spegni le luci.

items.note: Separable: turn it on / turn it off. Also switch on / off.

items.n: attaccare / staccare (presa)

ex.t: Plug the fridge in before you fill it. Unplug the toaster at night.
ex.n: Attacca il frigo prima di riempirlo. Stacca il tostapane di notte.

items.note: Plug / outlet / wall socket. In Canada 110 V, like the US.

items.n: ritirare, raccogliere, andare a prendere

ex.t: Can you pick up some milk on your way home?
ex.n: Puoi prendere del latte quando torni a casa?

items.note: Pick up a package / pick up Sofia / pick up the garbage. Also pick up the phone = rispondere.

items.n: mettere a posto, riordinare

ex.t: Put the dishes away before you go out.
ex.n: Metti via i piatti prima di uscire.

items.note: Put away = restore to its place. Put down = posare. Put off = rimandare.

items.n: buttare via

ex.t: Don't throw out the boxes — Sofia wants them for storage.
ex.n: Non buttare le scatole — Sofia le vuole per gli armadi.

items.note: Separable. Also chuck out (informal, UK).

items.n: guastarsi, rompersi

ex.t: The dishwasher broke down in week two.
ex.n: La lavastoviglie si è rotta la seconda settimana.

items.note: Intransitive. Also: a person breaks down = crolla.

items.n: riparare, aggiustare

ex.t: Vince came at 7 a.m. and fixed the igniter in ten minutes.
ex.n: Vince è venuto alle 7 e ha riparato l'accenditore in dieci minuti.

items.note: Also repair. Fix is more common in North American English.

items.n: controllare, dare un'occhiata

ex.t: I asked Franco to look over the boiler room last month.
ex.n: Ho chiesto a Franco di controllare il locale caldaia il mese scorso.

items.note: Look over = inspect carefully. Different from look up (cercare), look after (prendersi cura), look out (attenzione).

items.n: occuparsi di, gestire

ex.t: The landlord will deal with the pest problem.
ex.n: Si occuperà il proprietario del problema parassiti.

items.note: Inseparable. Also handle, take care of.

sections.title: Past perfect and reported requests
sections.intro: Three pieces: the past perfect, the key tense of B1; past perfect vs past simple with by the time, after, before, already, never before; and reported requests and orders (she asked me to…, she told me not to…). The passive form have / get something done at the end as a preview.

blocks.title: Past perfect: had + participle
blocks.rule: The past before another past: English I had done, I had gone. One form for every person: had + past participle. The contraction 'd (I'd, you'd, he'd, she'd, we'd, they'd) is standard in speech and informal writing — be careful: 'd can also be would (I'd like, I'd go), so look at the next word. Negative: hadn't + participle (I hadn't understood). Question: Had you + participle? (Had you signed before?). Use the past perfect: (1) for a prior action in a past narrative (when I arrived, she had already left); (2) after by the time (by the time Vince got there, we'd been cold for seven hours); (3) with never…before, ever…before, already, yet (I had never signed a lease before); (4) in reported speech when the original was past simple or present perfect (he said he had seen it = he said «I saw it» or «I've seen it»); (5) in the third conditional (unit 20) — if I had known, I would have called. The past perfect continuous (had been doing) is for duration up to a past moment: I'd been waiting for an hour when they called me.

blocks.caption: The past perfect of sign — one form for all persons
The two tenses in one story
head: Role
Tense
Example
rows: I arrived, I unlocked the door, I turned on the light.
When I arrived, Franco had already parked the van and had carried in the boxes.
duration up to a past moment
I'd been living with Sofia for three weeks when the furnace died.
I hadn't read the lease properly. We hadn't seen the alley neighbour yet.
Had you signed a lease before? Had she called the plumber?

items.t: By the time Vince arrived, we'd been cold for seven hours. We'd opened the taps, we'd piled the blankets, and we'd gone to bed with hats on.
items.n: Quando Vince è arrivato, avevamo freddo da sette ore. Avevamo aperto i rubinetti, ammucchiato le coperte, e messo a letto con il cappello.

items.t: She told me she had never signed a lease on her own before — her parents had always done it.
items.n: Mi disse che non aveva mai firmato un contratto da sola — i genitori l'avevano sempre fatto.

items.t: After I had read the lease, I signed it. After reading it, I signed it. (both are fine)
items.n: Dopo che avevo letto il contratto, l'ho firmato. Dopo averlo letto, l'ho firmato.
items.note: After + past perfect, or after + ing (same subject). The second is lighter.

items.t: By 11 p.m. the thermostat had dropped to 14, Sofia had put on her parka, and I'd started texting the landlord.
items.n: Alle 23 il termostato era sceso a 14, Sofia aveva messo il parka e io avevo iniziato a scrivere al proprietario.
items.note: Three past perfects after by + time. The sequence is already stacked up.

items.wrong: When I arrived, Franco already parked.
items.right: When I arrived, Franco had already parked.
items.why: Prior action in the past → past perfect.

items.wrong: I was reading the lease for three days.
items.right: I'd been reading the lease for three days.
items.why: Duration up to a past moment → past perfect continuous.

items.wrong: She had never signed a lease — now she signs one.
items.right: She had never signed a lease — then she signed one.
items.why: The past perfect lives inside a past story. If the frame is the present, use the present perfect: she has never signed a lease.

items.wrong: I'd like a coffee = I had like a coffee?
items.right: I'd like = I would like (conditional). I'd signed = I had signed (past perfect).
items.why: The contraction 'd can be would or had. The next verb tells you: 'd + base → would, 'd + participle → had.

items.wrong: By the time they called, we waited for an hour.
items.right: By the time they called, we'd been waiting for an hour.
items.why: By the time triggers the past perfect (or past perfect continuous for duration).

blocks.title: Reported requests and orders
blocks.rule: English reports requests and orders with the pattern verb + object + to + infinitive. The direct speech «Please text me» becomes she asked me to text her. The direct «Don't call» becomes she told me not to call. The verbs: ask (polite request), tell (order), remind (reminder), warn (warning), advise (advice), beg (strong plea), order (strict), invite (invitation), encourage (support), expect (anticipate). The negative uses not before to: he told me not to flush paper. The pronouns shift: me → her, you → me, your → my. This is a quieter grammar than reported statements and questions (which backshift the tenses, unit 19), but you use it in every conversation about what happened: she asked me to…, she told me to…, I told them not to…

blocks.caption: Direct → reported
head: Direct speech
Reported
rows: She asked me to text her, and not to call.
She told me not to flush any paper.
«Could you look over the boiler room?»
She asked Franco to look over the boiler room.
She advised us to open the taps a trickle.
She warned me not to try the oven trick.
She reminded me to pay first and last.
«Would you mind leaving your boots at the door?»
She asked us to leave our boots at the door.
She told us to give 60 days' notice before moving out.

items.t: Mrs. Oyelaran asked me to text, not to call. She told me not to flush any paper. She reminded me to pay first and last on the first.
items.n: La signora Oyelaran mi ha chiesto di scrivere, non chiamare. Mi ha detto di non buttare carta. Mi ha ricordato di pagare primo e ultimo mese il primo del mese.
items.note: Three reports in a row, three different verbs: asked (polite), told (direct), reminded (memory).

items.t: I asked Franco to look over the boiler room, and he said the vents were fine.
items.n: Ho chiesto a Franco di controllare il locale caldaia, e ha detto che le prese d'aria erano a posto.
items.note: The second half is a reported statement (unit 19): the vents are → were.

items.t: «Could you please let us know what to do?» → She asked him to let them know what to do.
items.n: «Può farci sapere cosa fare?» → Gli chiese di far sapere cosa fare.

blocks.title: The Italian equivalent
blocks.text: Italian uses chiedere / dire + di + infinito: she asked me to go = [[mi ha chiesto di andare]]; she told me not to flush = [[mi ha detto di non tirare lo sciacquone]]. The structure is the same shape (verb + object + preposition + infinitive) but the preposition is to in English, di in Italian. Same subject in Italian takes the infinitive; English can keep it or switch to a that-clause (she said she would go).

items.wrong: She asked me that I text her.
items.right: She asked me to text her.
items.why: Ask + object + to + infinitive, not a that-clause.

items.wrong: She told to me to leave.
items.why: Told takes the object directly, without to (unlike said).

items.right: She asked me not to call.
items.why: Negative = not + to-inf.

items.right: She told me to go. / She said «Go»., / She said to go. (less common)
items.why: Said doesn't take an object like told. Use told for the reported order.

blocks.title: Have / get something done
blocks.rule: The construction have + object + past participle means to arrange for someone else to do something: I had the furnace fixed = qualcuno la ha riparata per me. Form: have (any tense) + object + past participle. Also get + object + past participle, more informal: I got the lock changed. English uses this all the time where Italian uses farsi + infinito (farsi tagliare i capelli, farsi riparare la macchina) or the passive. Common contexts: hair, car, house, laundry, bills, taxes. B1 just needs the shape and five examples.

blocks.caption: Have / get something done
head: Pattern
Example
rows: I had the furnace fixed yesterday.
I got my hair cut on Saturday.
She had the pipes checked last month.
We're going to have the walls painted.
I haven't had the car serviced yet.

items.t: I had the furnace fixed, I had the lock changed, and I had the walls painted. All in one week.
items.n: Mi sono fatta riparare la caldaia, cambiare la serratura e dipingere le pareti. Tutto in una settimana.

items.t: You should get your eyes checked once a year.
items.n: Dovresti farti controllare gli occhi una volta all'anno.

items.t: She's having her kitchen done. The contractor started last Monday.
items.n: Si sta facendo rifare la cucina. L'impresa ha iniziato lunedì.

items.wrong: I have fixed the furnace. (I did it myself) vs I had the furnace fixed. (someone did it for me)
items.right: Both are grammatical; they mean different things.
items.why: Word order: subject + have + object + participle = someone did it for the subject. Subject + have + participle (no object before) = subject's own completed action.

items.wrong: I had the furnace to fix.
items.why: Past participle, not infinitive.

items.q: Write a six-sentence paragraph about moving into a place last year, using at least two past perfects, one past simple, one reported request (she / he asked / told me…), one phrasal verb (move in, set up, break down…) and one Ontario rental word.

sections.title: The standard lease, hydro, and the second-hand city
sections.intro: What a tenant in Ontario needs to know, in two pages: the standard lease, utilities, waste pickup, the second-hand economy around a basement rental.

blocks.text: Since April 2018, Ontario has required every private landlord to use the same residential tenancy agreement, a thirteen-page government form you can download for free. It fixes the main terms (rent, utilities included, parking, pets, no smoking, access) and attaches the [[Residential Tenancies Act]] in plain language. Rent control is tied to the [[annual guideline]] (around 2–3% most years, set by the province); for units first occupied after 15 November 2018 there is no cap. [[First and last month's rent]] up front is the standard deposit, with no [[damage deposit]] allowed by law. The landlord must give [[24 hours' notice]] in writing to enter, except for emergencies; the tenant must give [[60 days' notice]] to leave at the end of the term. Disputes go to the [[Landlord and Tenant Board]] (LTB), a provincial tribunal that moves slowly in both directions. Advice is free from [[Steps to Justice]] (stepstojustice.ca) and from the [[tenant rights lines]] of CLEO and the ACTO. Chiara's basement is nothing special in Toronto — half the city rents the top or bottom half of a house — and the lease is the same in Rosedale and in Bloordale.

[[Hydro]] (electricity, from the old name Ontario Hydro, around since the dams on the Niagara) is billed by [[Toronto Hydro]] or a local utility and often included in a basement rental. [[Gas]] (for the furnace and the stove) is [[Enbridge]]; [[water]] is the city. If utilities are not included, budget around $100–200 a month in winter for a one-bedroom. [[Time-of-use pricing]] charges less on evenings and weekends, so Toronto laundry is nocturnal. If you forget a bill, [[collections]] come fast; if the hydro is cut off between November and April, a tenant can call the [[Low-Income Energy Assistance Program]] (LEAP). [[Smart meter]], [[peak hours]], [[baseboard heater]] and [[forced-air gas furnace]] are the four Ontario words a tenant learns in their first winter.

blocks.title: Garbage day, blue bin, green bin
blocks.text: Toronto has four bins: grey ([[garbage]], every two weeks), blue ([[recycling]], every two weeks), green ([[organics]], the famous Toronto green bin, every week), and yard waste (every two weeks, seasonal). Pickup is on a fixed day; the bins go out the night before, come back in the next morning. The bylaw fines are small but real. Christmas trees have their own January week. Furniture is picked up [[by appointment]] for free, through 311. If you want to [[get rid of]] a sofa quickly, [[Facebook Marketplace]] and [[Bunz]] work in a day; [[Kijiji]] still exists for the rest. The second-hand economy is huge: IKEA for new, [[Habitat for Humanity ReStore]] for restored, Facebook and Bunz for personal transfers, and the sidewalk on Thursday night for everything else. Chiara's whole bedroom came from the alley, and that is not an unusual story.
Hydro, hoop and the English of a basement

Three register tips for a tenant. One, texts to the landlord are polite but not formal: [[Hi Mrs. Oyelaran, sorry to text at this hour, the furnace just died.]] The three parts are hello, apology for the hour, specific fact. Two, formal emails use blocks you can memorise: [[Dear … , I am writing with regard to… · at approximately… · as instructed · attended the premises · I would be grateful if you could… · Please find attached · Best regards, …]]. Three, the vocabulary of a basement is a small world you learn fast: [[the furnace, the breaker, the thermostat, the vents, the panel, the water heater, the sump pump, the laundry chute, the alley neighbour]]. If you can say those nine things, you can run a basement in Toronto.
